findings.issue: No A14 effector is registered for distribution.run.approve, distribution.propose, manual_payout, restore_lines, declare_reduced or exit.approve, and A16's journalPostcondition is never registered. Under A14 an approval that stays in 'approved' expires 72 h after submission, and A16 refuses postings on an expired approval. A06's MRN01 run (APR-2289 approved 23 Sep, paid 10 Oct) could never post steps 2-5. The precheck also says 'sponsor_signoff_approval_id is approved', which fails once the request moves on to confirmed or closed.
findings.fix: Add an effector table: for each A40 action code, its registerEffector {execute, revert, postcondition}. run.approve: execute = in_review -> approved plus registerApprovedFile; postcondition = A16 journalPostcondition. propose: execute = calculated -> in_review. Check the sign-off as 'decided approve (approved..closed)', as A03's linked_approval_approved does. Add a challenge: an approval decided more than 72 h before execution still posts.

findings.issue: A16's approved-file binding needs A40 to call registerApprovedFile(approval_id, canonical_file) before the first journal, and it takes 'the funded gross' and 'the approved file's remainder' from the file. A40 never calls it, and A40's CSV header has no remainder, run net or funded-gross field, so A16 cannot validate step 3 or LDG_RUN_TOTAL_MISMATCH.
findings.fix: Add registerApprovedFile to the approved -> funding effector (idempotent). Extend the canonical file with a run trailer row (or fixed columns) carrying net_cents, remainder_cents, carry_in total and funded_gross_cents, agreed with A16. Add a test that A16 accepts step 3 and refuses a remainder that is off by one cent.

findings.issue: A16's distribution.pay_bank row accepts only lines that are closed_account or manual_payout in the approved file. A line that exhausts its retries has exception_code null in the approved file, which cannot be changed after approval, so its manual payout is refused. The run stays in 'retrying' for ever, and the 'Retry that pays twice' challenge cannot pass.
findings.fix: Reopen A16 so that pay_bank accepts any line of the approved file whose step 4 journal was never consumed, when a per-line distribution.line.manual_payout approval exists. Or define the retry-exhausted path another way that A16 accepts. Add the case to the challenge and the pass criteria.

findings.issue: A40 requires the rent-roll import and the attestation to be 'for the same period'. A06 builds the September runs from the attested August rent roll, and A34's own test approves the September distribution against the August attestation. The seeded BAY01, MRN01 and HAW01 September runs (and the SPN-09 and DF-A40-01 fixtures) therefore cannot be created. A34 also has no 'accepted total' on RentRollImport; the total is the attestation's rent_collected_cents.
findings.fix: State the arrears convention: an income period for month M distributes the rent roll and attestation of month M-1 (or a configured offset). Read gross_rent_cents from A34's attestation rent_roll item (rent_collected_cents) through index.ts. Update the G19 precheck and the BAY01 challenge.

findings.issue: The record-date certification collides with A18's supersession rule: 'a later certification row for the same vehicle and month supersedes it'. Once the month-end version is certified (a REGO task on the first business day), the 23 Sep record-date version becomes 'superseded'. A40's snapshot_certified precheck (version 'certified') then fails for any run submitted after that, which covers BAY01's usual early-October timeline. Certifying a record-date version after month-end would instead supersede the month-end certification.
findings.fix: Make snapshot_certified pass when a register_certification row covers register_version_id, whether the version is certified or superseded. Also reopen A18 so that supersession is keyed by as_of, not by month. Add a challenge: month-end certification lands between the lock and the submit.

findings.issue: A40 says it registers DistributionFundingProvider 'through A17's index.ts', but A17 is not an ancestor of A40 in app-graph.json. A17's spec says 'Registered by A49 ... if the graph gains an A40 -> A17 edge, A40 registers it instead'. As written, the build breaks the module boundary lint or double-registers.
findings.fix: Add A17 as a dependency of A40 (A17 is AM1, so there is no cycle) and update the Depends-on line. Or export the implementation from A40's index.ts and leave registration to A49, as A17 says. Keep the 'Sponsor funding matched' challenge on the chosen path.

findings.issue: A14 has no 'rejection effector'. A reject only writes the outbox event approval.rejected, and expiry writes approval.expired. A40 never consumes either, and it does not say what happens when run.approve, propose or fund expires or is cancelled. A run whose run.approve expires is stuck in in_review (the only exit is a CFO rejection).
findings.fix: Specify an outbox consumer for approval.rejected, approval.expired and approval.cancelled on each A40 action code. Rejected run.approve -> in_review -> draft (actor = the deciding CFO). Expired or cancelled -> the run stays in its state, a resubmit is allowed and a new id is issued. Test each case.

findings.issue: The submit precheck exceptions_confirmed needs a FINA confirmation per exception line (exception_confirmed_by). No route, column (it is missing from distribution_lines), action id or G22 row exists for it, and A74's ADM-19 has no confirm action. Any run with an AML hold, closed account or dust line can never be submitted.
findings.fix: Add exception_confirmed_by and exception_confirmed_at to distribution_lines. Add POST /v1/distributions/runs/{id}/exceptions/confirm with action id M12.exception.confirm (FINA; decide whether a staff agent may confirm and record it), a G22 row and a parity-manifest entry. Or state that submit by the human FINA confirms all exceptions.

findings.issue: restore-lines rewrites the non-execution columns of lines after 'approved', but A40's own trigger refuses every non-execution column from 'approved' on, so the restore cannot run. The tamper challenge ('the one that slips through in a copy without the trigger') is also inconsistent, because a holder_ref change is refused by the trigger too.
findings.fix: Define a trigger bypass limited to the restore effector (a session variable set only inside the approved restore_lines effector transaction, audited). Rewrite the tamper challenge: disable the trigger explicitly in the harness for the hash-path trials.

findings.issue: The distribution.propose row is registered as 'always' SP-FIN -> SP-OWN, but A14 line 39 says sponsor rows naming SP-OWN fall back to RealX PART or SECO when tenant_owner_count = 1, and A40's own text says 'or policy names RealX PART'. A03's sponsor_owner_approved guard accepts only SP-OWN. A14's exhaustive-rows seed test and the one-person-sponsor challenge give conflicting results.
findings.fix: Pick one rule. Either register an explicit tenant_owner_count = 1 row with no fallback (refused DST_SPONSOR_SIGNOFF_REQUIRED) and record the deviation from A14's fallback, or register a PART fallback row plus a named A03 guard extension. Test both counts.

findings.issue: The aml_hold visibility rule depends on 'A11's need-to-know check' for FINA and CFO on their own runs, and A11 defines no such check.
findings.fix: Define the check in A40: the principal (or the agent's human) is the maker or a required checker or decider on this run's A14 requests. Test FINA and CFO on another run being masked.
